name: azure-data-explorer
label: Azure Data Explorer
description: Azure Data Explorer is a fully managed, high-performance big data analytics platform that makes it easy to analyze large volumes of data streamed from applications, websites, IoT devices, and more, in real-time. This connector connects to Azure Data Explorer (Kusto) clusters using the Azure Data Explorer REST APIs and Kusto Query Language (KQL). It allows you to list databases and tables, explore table schemas and data, run custom KQL queries and management (control) commands, and write data back to the database by ingesting records inline, as well as delete records or tables from the database. This connector is useful for security investigations and enrichment of data, for example, viewing security logs and updating metrics back to the database.

operations.title: Run Query
operations.description: Runs a Kusto Query Language (KQL) query on the specified database on the Azure Data Explorer cluster and retrieves the results. For example, you can use this operation to view security logs for investigations and enrichment. If the specified query is a control command (starts with a dot '.'), such as .show tables, then it is automatically executed on the management endpoint.

parameters.title: Query
parameters.description: Specify the Kusto Query Language (KQL) query to run on the database. For example, MyTable | where Severity == 'High' | take 10
parameters.name: query
parameters.tooltip: Specify the KQL query to run on the database.

parameters.title: Database
parameters.description: Specify the name of the database on which you want to run this operation.
parameters.name: database
parameters.tooltip: Name of the database on which you want to run this operation.

parameters.title: Query Timeout
parameters.description: (Optional) Specify the maximum time to wait for the query to complete, in the HH:MM:SS format. By default, this is set to 00:03:00, i.e., 3 minutes.
parameters.name: query_timeout
parameters.tooltip: (Optional) Maximum time to wait for the query to complete, in the HH:MM:SS format. By default, this is set to 00:03:00.

parameters.title: Database

parameters.title: Database

parameters.name: database

operations.title: Get Table Data
operations.description: Retrieves rows from a specified table in the database based on the specified time range, filter query, sort order, and the maximum number of records to retrieve. You can use this operation to view security logs for investigations and enrichment.

parameters.title: Table Name
parameters.description: Specify the name of the table from which you want to retrieve the data.
parameters.name: table
parameters.tooltip: Name of the table from which you want to retrieve the data.

parameters.title: Database
parameters.description: Specify the name of the database on which you want to run this operation.
parameters.name: database
parameters.tooltip: Name of the database on which you want to run this operation.

parameters.title: Time Column
parameters.description: (Optional) Specify the name of the datetime column in the table based on which you want to filter the data, such as a Timestamp column. If specified, then also specify the Time From and Time To parameters.
parameters.name: time_column
parameters.tooltip: (Optional) Name of the datetime column based on which you want to filter the data. If specified, then also specify the Time From and Time To parameters.

parameters.title: Time From
parameters.description: (Optional) Specify the start datetime in the YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS format from which to retrieve the data. This parameter is used only if the Time Column parameter is specified.
parameters.name: time_from
parameters.tooltip: (Optional) Start datetime in the YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS format from which to retrieve the data. This parameter is used only if the Time Column parameter is specified.

parameters.title: Time To
parameters.description: (Optional) Specify the end datetime in the YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS format until which to retrieve the data. This parameter is used only if the Time Column parameter is specified.
parameters.name: time_to
parameters.tooltip: (Optional) End datetime in the YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS format until which to retrieve the data. This parameter is used only if the Time Column parameter is specified.

parameters.title: Filter
parameters.description: (Optional) Specify the KQL filter query to apply to the data retrieved from the table, without the pipe symbol. For example, where Severity == 'High'
parameters.name: filter
parameters.tooltip: (Optional) KQL filter query to apply to the data retrieved from the table, without the pipe symbol. For example, where Severity == 'High'

parameters.title: Order By
parameters.description: (Optional) Specify the column and sort order, asc or desc, based on which you want to sort the data retrieved from the table. For example, Timestamp desc
parameters.name: order_by
parameters.tooltip: (Optional) Column and sort order, asc or desc, based on which you want to sort the data retrieved from the table.

parameters.title: Limit
parameters.description: (Optional) Specify the maximum number of records that this operation should retrieve from the table. If not specified, all records matching the filter criteria are retrieved.
parameters.name: limit
parameters.tooltip: (Optional) Maximum number of records that this operation should retrieve from the table. If not specified, all records matching the filter criteria are retrieved.

parameters.title: Query Timeout
parameters.description: (Optional) Specify the maximum time to wait for the query to complete, in the HH:MM:SS format. By default, this is set to 00:03:00, i.e., 3 minutes.
parameters.name: query_timeout
parameters.tooltip: (Optional) Maximum time to wait for the query to complete, in the HH:MM:SS format. By default, this is set to 00:03:00.

operations.title: Ingest Inline Data
operations.description: Writes (ingests) records into a specified table in the database using the .ingest inline control command. Specify the data to ingest in the CSV format. You can use this operation to update data or metrics back to the database.

parameters.title: Table Name
parameters.description: Specify the name of the table into which you want to ingest the data. The table must already exist in the database.
parameters.name: table
parameters.tooltip: Name of the table into which you want to ingest the data. The table must already exist in the database.

parameters.title: CSV Data
parameters.description: Specify the data, in the CSV format, to ingest into the table. Each line is one record with comma-separated values. The values must match the order of the columns in the table and must be compatible with the column data types. Do not include a header row; column names are not read by this command. Use a new line for each new record.
parameters.name: csv_data
parameters.tooltip: Data, in the CSV format, to ingest into the table. Each line is one record. The values must match the order of the columns in the table. Do not include a header row.
parameters.placeholder:
E.g. For a table with columns (Timestamp, Severity, Message):
2024-01-01 00:00:00,High,Login failed
2024-01-01 00:05:00,Low,Login successful

parameters.title: Database
parameters.description: Specify the name of the database on which you want to run this operation.
parameters.name: database
parameters.tooltip: Name of the database on which you want to run this operation.

operations.title: Delete Table Data
operations.description: Deletes records from a specified table in the database that match the specified filter conditions using the .delete table records control command. This is a soft delete: the matching records are immediately hidden from queries and are physically removed when the affected extents are rebuilt during background compaction. Requires Table Admin permission on the database.

parameters.title: Table Name
parameters.description: Specify the name of the table from which you want to delete the data.
parameters.name: table
parameters.tooltip: Name of the table from which you want to delete the data.

parameters.title: Predicate
parameters.description: Specify the filter conditions, starting with the where clause, for the records to delete from the table. For example, where Severity == 'Low'. If the column name contains spaces or special characters, enclose it in square brackets, e.g. where ['Connector Name'] == 'Azure Data Explorer'. The specified conditions are applied on the table specified in the Table Name field.
parameters.name: predicate
parameters.tooltip: Filter conditions, starting with the where clause, for the records to delete from the table. For example, where Severity == 'Low'. Enclose column names containing spaces in square brackets.
parameters.placeholder: E.g. where Severity == 'Low' or where ['Column Name'] == 'value'

parameters.title: Database
parameters.description: Specify the name of the database on which you want to run this operation.
parameters.name: database
parameters.tooltip: Name of the database on which you want to run this operation.

operations.title: Delete Table
operations.description: Deletes a specified table, along with its data, from the database using the .drop table control command.

parameters.title: Table Name
parameters.description: Specify the name of the table that you want to delete from the database.
parameters.name: table
parameters.tooltip: Name of the table that you want to delete from the database.

parameters.title: Database
parameters.description: Specify the name of the database on which you want to run this operation.
parameters.name: database
parameters.tooltip: Name of the database on which you want to run this operation.
